facts: 1840 census: head of a household of nine, Casey County
1850 census: labourer, Rockcastle County, born Virginia
1860 census: age 66, Rockcastle County, with son Samuel (26)
people.name: Elijah Giles
people.role: The patriarch — the first Giles in the records
people.bio: Born in Virginia around 1794, Elijah came west on the great migration that filled Kentucky after statehood. By 1840 he was heading a household of nine in Casey County. In 1850 the census-taker found him in Rockcastle County, a 56-year-old labourer living right next door to his son James — and in 1860, at 66, he was still in Rockcastle with his son Samuel at his side.

people.name: Susan Giles
people.bio: Susan, like her husband, was born in Virginia. In 1850 she kept the Rockcastle County home where children Nancy, Allen, Samuel and Vienna still lived.

people.name: Samuel Giles
people.bio: Samuel was a teenage farm hand in his father’s 1850 household and was still living with Elijah in Rockcastle County in 1860.

facts: 1850: farmer, real estate worth $300, Rockcastle County
1870: farmer, Neatsville district, Adair County — ten under one roof
people.name: James W. Giles
people.place: Rockcastle County → Neatsville, Adair County, KY
people.role: The farmer who brought the family to Adair County
people.bio: James W. Giles was a 26-year-old farmer in Rockcastle County in 1850, living between his father Elijah and the Prindle family. By 1870 he and Abby had moved the family west to the Neatsville district of Adair County, where a houseful of sons worked the farm beside him. He was still farming at 58 in 1880, and he died on 19 June 1913, at 88, and was buried in the Tabernacle Cemetery at Neatsville.

people.name: Abigail “Abby” C. Giles
people.role: Wife of James W. — born a Prindle
people.bio: Abby was born in Virginia. In 1850 she was 21, with a year-old son, John, and her Prindle kin lived on the very next farm. She raised a large family and kept house in Neatsville through 1880.

people.name: John P. Giles
people.bio: The eldest — a baby on the 1850 census, working the farm at 21 in 1870.

people.name: Elijah F. Giles
people.bio: Named for his grandfather. Working the farm at 14 in 1870; a house painter, married to Eliza, still under his father’s roof in 1880.

people.name: Benjamin F. Giles
people.bio: Ten years old and working on the farm in 1870; a 19-year-old house painter in 1880.

people.name: Alice Giles
people.bio: Eight years old in 1870; at home at 18 in 1880.

people.name: Perry G. Giles
people.bio: Five years old in the 1870 Neatsville household.

people.name: Anna Giles
people.bio: The baby of 1870, age 3; “Annie” at 13 in 1880.

people.name: Deray Giles
people.bio: Farming at 16 in his father’s 1880 household.

people.name: Jane Giles
people.bio: Twelve years old, at home, in 1880.

facts: 1900: head of household, Pellyton district — next door to James Washington Giles
Father of Luther, Arthur Owen and Melcena
people.name: William Preston Giles
people.bio: Born in March 1851, Preston — William P. on the census — was a 19-year-old working his father’s farm in 1870. He married Susan around 1881 and by 1900 was heading his own home in the Pellyton district with sons Luther and Arthur Owen and daughter Melcena. His next-door neighbor was James Washington Giles, who had grown up in the same Neatsville household.

people.name: Susan F. Giles
people.bio: Born in July 1858, Susan married Preston around 1881. In 1900 she reported three children born, all three living: Luther, Arthur Owen and Melcena. Luther’s 1959 obituary named her proudly: “son of the late Preston and Susan Giles.”

facts: 1880: head of household, Casey Creek (written “K. W.”)
people.name: James Washington Giles
people.role: Of the 1870 Neatsville household — grandfather of Henry Earl Giles
people.bio: Called simply “Washington” at 17 on the 1870 farm, he had his own home in the Casey Creek district by 1880 — where the census-taker wrote him down as “K. W. Giles” — with wife Mary and little Milton. In 1900 he lived next door to Preston at Pellyton. He died at Knifley on 21 July 1938.

facts: 1900: Pellyton district; four children, all living
people.name: Mary E. (Sanders) Giles
people.bio: Mary E. Sanders married James Washington in the mid-1870s. In 1900 she reported four children born, all four living. Her son Frank’s 1982 obituary remembered his parents as “James Washington and Mary Sanders Giles.”

facts: Married Nora Allen in Tennessee, September 1906
1950 census: farm at Blue Hollow, Ky 76, with Nora and sons Walter, Russell, Elvin
Died 22 January 1959 at home, Neatsville community
people.name: Luther Aaron Giles
people.place: Pellyton · Knifley · Neatsville, Adair County, KY
people.bio: Born in August 1882, Luther grew up on his father Preston’s farm at Pellyton. In September 1906 the Knifley news column reported that “Mr. Luther Giles and Miss Tinna Allen eloped to Tennessee a few days ago, and got married.” Luther and Nora raised seven sons and two daughters on Adair County farmland — Blue Hollow, off Ky 76, in 1950 — and by 1959 their children were spread from Adair County to Indiana and Ohio. A retired farmer and a member of the Tabernacle Christian Church, he died at his home in the Neatsville community on 22 January 1959, and was laid to rest in the Tabernacle Cemetery.

facts: Married Luther Giles in Tennessee, September 1906
Died 9 May 1975, Louisville, age 85; buried Tabernacle Cemetery
people.name: Nora V. (Allen) Giles
people.bio: Nora Victoria Allen was born on 23 January 1890 in Adair County, the daughter of Thomas Allen and Mary Bett White, and was known to family as “Tiny” (the 1906 Knifley column printed it “Tinna”). She married Luther Giles in Tennessee in September 1906, raised nine children, and was still keeping the Blue Hollow farm with Luther in 1950. A member of the Tabernacle Christian Church and a Knifley resident, she died in Louisville on 9 May 1975, at 85. She rests in the Tabernacle Cemetery.

people.name: Arthur Owen Giles
people.bio: Luther’s younger brother, born July 1884. “Owen” made his home at Dunnville and died at 82 on 29 June 1967 — a native Adair Countian to the end. His pallbearers were a roll-call of Giles men.

people.name: Melcena (Giles) Blair
people.bio: Preston and Susan’s daughter, born January 1888. She married Brigham Tilden Blair and raised a large family. She died at her daughter’s home in Knifley on 13 December 1962, age 74, and was buried at Salem Cemetery in Casey County.

facts: 1920: Pellyton with Bessie and son Henry
Rived 10,000 shingles for Henry & Janice’s log house
people.name: Thomas Franklin “Frank” Giles
people.role: Luther’s Pellyton neighbor — Henry Earl’s father
people.bio: Born 22 November 1889, Frank grew up next door to Luther’s family at Pellyton in 1900. When his son Henry and daughter-in-law Janice Holt Giles built their log house at Spout Springs, Frank rived the roof shingles by hand: ten thousand of them, according to the house’s National Register nomination. He died 5 May 1982.

people.name: Bessie H. (Bottoms) Giles
people.bio: Bessie Hazel Bottoms married Frank Giles. During the war she wrote letters to her son’s sweetheart, Janice — letters that survive in Janice Holt Giles’s papers at Western Kentucky University.

people.name: Milton Gaither Giles
people.bio: A two-year-old on the 1880 Casey Creek census — his father’s first son.

people.name: Mahala Jane Giles
people.bio: The newborn of the 1880 Casey Creek household.

people.name: Jared L. Giles
people.bio: Born August 1883; a 16-year-old in his father’s 1900 Pellyton home.

people.name: Zackie Giles
people.role: Child of Luther & Nora — Joshua’s great-uncle
people.bio: The first son named in his father’s obituary. In 1950 he lived with his own family in the same Casey Creek census district as his parents and brothers.

people.name: Van Giles
people.role: Child of Luther & Nora — Joshua’s great-uncle
people.bio: Named among the seven sons in 1959, living in Adair County.

people.name: G. Walter Giles
people.role: Child of Luther & Nora — Joshua’s great-uncle
people.bio: Walter served in World War II — at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri, in November 1942, and stationed in Virginia as a Pfc. in June 1945, when his sisters Flossie and Melzena travelled to see him. In 1950 he was back on the Blue Hollow farm with his parents.

people.name: Elvin L. Giles
people.role: Child of Luther & Nora — Joshua’s great-uncle
people.bio: The youngest boy on the 1950 Blue Hollow farm. By 1959 he lived in Columbus, Indiana.

people.name: Russell A. Giles
people.role: Child of Luther & Nora — Joshua’s great-uncle
people.bio: On the home farm in 1950; by 1959 he had gone north to Wadsworth, Ohio.

people.name: Herman W. Giles
people.role: Child of Luther & Nora — Joshua’s great-uncle
people.bio: In 1950 he lived with his sister Melzena’s family, a few farms from William, with his wife Rena and their baby.

people.name: Flossie (Giles) Burton
people.role: Child of Luther & Nora — Joshua’s great-aunt
people.bio: Mrs. Flossie Burton. In June 1945 she and her sister set off for Virginia to visit their soldier brother Walter. By 1959 she lived in Columbus, Indiana.

people.name: Melzena (Giles) Farmer
people.role: Child of Luther & Nora — Joshua’s great-aunt
people.bio: Mrs. Leon Farmer. In 1950 her household in the Casey Creek district included her brother Herman. By 1959 the Farmers had moved to Wadsworth, Ohio. She died before her mother, Nora, in 1975.

facts: Pvt., Co. E, 9th Infantry — Rifleman (745), Army serial 35806948
Wounded in action, France, 3 August 1944 — Purple Heart
Honorable discharge, William Beaumont General Hospital, El Paso, 30 May 1945
Died 16 March 2001; buried Heavenly Hill Cemetery, Columbia, KY
people.name: William Cecil Giles
people.place: Knifley, KY · Wadsworth, OH · Edinburg, IN · Edmonton, KY
people.bio: Born at Knifley on 19 April 1924, William grew up on his parents’ farm and was farming himself when the war came. He was inducted into the Army in October 1943, served as a rifleman with Company E, 9th Infantry, and was badly wounded in the legs in France on 3 August 1944. Purple Heart. He married Bertha Burton in the spring of 1945 and came home to Adair County on 1 June 1945. He went where the work was: Wadsworth, Ohio in 1949 and Edinburg, Indiana by 1959. Later he retired from Cosco Industries, and in his later years lived at Edmonton, Kentucky. A Baptist, he died at Glasgow on 16 March 2001, at 77, survived by ten children, twenty grandchildren and five great-grandchildren, and rests at Heavenly Hill Cemetery in Columbia.

facts: Daughter of Mr. & Mrs. John R. Burton
people.name: Bertha (Burton) Giles
people.place: Purdy community · Adair County, KY · Indiana
people.bio: Bertha was the daughter of John R. Burton. While William was overseas she was up in Indiana — the home paper placed “Miss Bertha Burton” at Edinburg in December 1944. By April 1945 she was Mrs. Bertha Giles, home visiting her parents. In 1950 she was 24, keeping house off Ky 206 near Luther and Nora’s farm, with two little girls, Evelyn and Bernadean. She and William raised eleven children, most of them born after the family settled in Johnson County, Indiana. Bertha died before William, and his 2001 obituary remembers her as his first wife, Bertha Burton Giles.

people.name: John R. Burton
people.bio: In April 1945 the Purdy column of the Adair County News reported that Mrs. Bertha Giles had spent a few days calling on her parents, Mr. and Mrs. John R. Burton.

people.name: Dular (Judd) Giles
people.bio: Dular Judd Giles was William’s wife in his later years at Edmonton. She survived him and died on 18 February 2003.

facts: Sergeant, U.S. Army, World War II
Died 1 October 1986; buried Caldwell Chapel, Knifley
people.name: Henry Earl Giles
people.place: Pellyton · Giles Ridge · Spout Springs, Adair County, KY
people.role: Of the Pellyton Giles — husband of novelist Janice Holt Giles
people.bio: Born in June 1916 and raised at Pellyton, Henry met Janice Holt on a two-day bus trip in 1943, then shipped out as a U.S. Army sergeant; hundreds of their wartime letters survive. They married on 11 October 1945, moved to the Giles Ridge farm on 30 May 1949, and later built the log house at Spout Springs — the house that had to be moved in 1967 when the Green River Lake came in. Henry published a novel of his own, Harbin’s Ridge (1951), and his war diary became The G.I. Journal of Sergeant Giles. He died 1 October 1986 and is buried at Caldwell Chapel, Knifley.

facts: Author of The Enduring Hills (1950) and 40 Acres and No Mule (1952)
Her papers are held at Western Kentucky University
people.name: Janice Holt Giles
people.bio: Arkansas-born Janice Holt married Henry Giles in 1945 and made his Adair County hills famous. From the farm on Giles Ridge and the log house at Spout Springs she published more than twenty books — The Enduring Hills, the Giles Ridge memoir 40 Acres and No Mule, The Kentuckians, Hannah Fowler, The Believers — and The Damned Engineers, a history of an Army engineer battalion in the Battle of the Bulge.

people.name: Robert Giles
people.bio: Henry’s brother; at home with Frank and Bessie in 1950.

people.name: Kenneth Giles
people.bio: Henry’s brother; at home with Frank and Bessie in 1950.

people.name: Irene (Giles) Scott
people.bio: Henry’s sister, named among his survivors in 1986.

people.name: Cora Mae (Giles) Rector
people.bio: Henry’s sister, named among his survivors in 1986.

people.name: Bertha Evelyn (Giles) Duncan
people.bio: The eldest of William and Bertha’s children, and her mother’s namesake. She was two years old on the 1950 census. Evelyn died before her father did in 2001, and she is remembered in the obituaries of her father and of her brothers Cecil and Hershel.

people.name: Bernadean (Giles) Myers
people.bio: William and Bertha’s second daughter, and the baby of the household on the 1950 census (written “Bernadine”). Hershel’s older sister, named among his survivors in 2022. Bernadean has since passed away, and she is remembered here with love.

people.name: William Ray Giles
people.bio: William Cecil’s son, remembered in his father’s 2001 obituary among the family members who had gone before him.

facts: Indian Creek High School, class of 1973: MVP and All-Conference in baseball and basketball
Owner, Cecil Giles Custom Homes (GA and IN), 30+ years
people.name: William Cecil “Cecil” Giles Jr.
people.bio: Born in Franklin, Indiana, on 16 December 1954, the fourth of William and Bertha’s eleven children and his father’s namesake. At Indian Creek High School (class of 1973) he starred in baseball and basketball: a pitcher and infielder on the sectional champions of 1971 and 1973, MVP and All-Conference in both sports, and the first Indian Creek athlete to earn a college scholarship in two sports. He earned a degree in education at Auburn University, taught and coached in the Cobb County schools of Marietta, Georgia, then built homes for more than thirty years as owner of Cecil Giles Custom Homes in Georgia and Indiana, retiring from Carpenters Union Local 301 in 2018. He lived in Nineveh and died on 15 August 2019, at 64, after a two-year fight with glioblastoma. His funeral was held in the Indian Creek gymnasium.

facts: Indian Creek High School, class of 1977; Building Trades at Ivy Tech
Self-employed framer: homes in Johnson, Morgan and Brown counties
Died 14 November 2022 at home in Martinsville, age 63
Funeral 19 November 2022, Meredith-Clark Funeral Home, Morgantown; buried East Hill Cemetery, Morgantown
people.role: Framer and builder — father of Shelby and Joshua
people.name: Hershel Dewayne Giles
people.bio: Hershel was born on 3 July 1959 in Franklin, Indiana, to William Cecil and Bertha (Burton) Giles. He graduated from Indian Creek High School in 1977 and studied Building Trades at Ivy Tech, then spent his working life as a self-employed framer, raising the walls of homes across Johnson, Morgan and Brown counties. He cruised in his 1972 Chevy Nova, boated and skied, hunted mushrooms, kept a vegetable garden and loved woodworking. He cheered for Dale Earnhardt Sr. and Chase Elliott on Sundays and for IU men’s basketball all winter, with his German shepherd Pal at his side. He loved his family, above all his children, Shelby and Joshua, and he was always the first to help anyone in need. A longtime Nineveh resident, he died at his home in Martinsville on 14 November 2022, at 63, and rests in East Hill Cemetery, Morgantown.

people.name: Danny Douglas
people.bio: Son of William Cecil and Bertha, and Hershel’s brother.

people.name: Alice Faye
people.bio: Daughter of William Cecil and Bertha, and Hershel’s sister. Alice kept her father’s 1945 Army discharge papers and gave them to her nephew Joshua. Those papers are the heart of the war chapter on this site.

people.name: Donna Sue
people.bio: Daughter of William Cecil and Bertha, and Hershel’s sister.

people.name: Jeanine
people.bio: Daughter of William Cecil and Bertha, and Hershel’s sister.

people.name: Joyce Christine
people.bio: Daughter of William Cecil and Bertha, and Hershel’s sister.

people.name: Shelby Nicole Giles
people.bio: Daughter of Hershel Dewayne Giles (1959–2022) and the elder of his two children — Joshua’s big sister.

people.name: Joshua Giles
people.bio: Son of Hershel Dewayne Giles (1959–2022) and younger brother of Shelby. His aunt Alice gave him his grandfather William’s Army discharge papers, and the family history on this site grew from them.
